text:
The Hurricanes had every excuse to look heavy-legged at Madison Square Garden. They'd played Edmonton the night before, a 7-4 win wrapped around Taylor Hall's 1,000th-game ceremony and Sebastian Aho's franchise goal record, and this was an early afternoon puck drop. For eight minutes it showed: Cory Lavalette of the North State Journal counted eight Rangers shots in the first eight, and called Carolina "a little loosey goosey."

Then the fourth line stepped in. Eric Robinson scored shorthanded at 13:00 of the first off a Jordan Staal feed, and Mika Zibanejad answered 72 seconds later, with a power-play tip-in set up by Adam Fox and J.T. Miller. The first period was dead even by expected goals (the quality of each side's chances), 1.24 to 1.31.

The second was where Carolina took the game. Jackson Blake's backhand at 13:13, set up by Hall and Logan Stankoven, swung the Hurricanes' win chance from 48% to 69%, the biggest single moment of the afternoon. Alexander Nikishin followed with a slap shot at 17:46 that had about a 4% chance of going in, and Sean Walker made it 4-1 at 18:27. Three goals in 5:14.

The Rangers kept getting power plays and kept using them: J.T. Miller scored on a 4% look in the third, their second goal on five chances. But at even strength Carolina won 3.01 to 1.94 in expected goals and outshot New York 41-27. Our replays of every shot gave the Hurricanes the win 57% of the time, so this wasn't a robbery, just a team that is very good at the parts of hockey that repeat. Jordan Martinook closed it at 17:38 off a Seth Jarvis pass, an assist for a player Lavalette noted is creating chances that aren't going in for him yet.

In net, Brandon Bussi stopped 25 of 27 and saved about 1.1 goals more than the shots deserved, including a 22% chance from Tye Kartye in the second. Dylan Garand made 36 saves at the other end, keeping out K'Andre Miller's best look of the third, and finished within half a goal of what the shots deserved. The Rangers' three-game winning streak is over, and with Igor Shesterkin out for the season, nights where the young goalie is asked to be perfect are going to keep coming.
headline: Five minutes in the second settle it for Carolina
